per_window.ps-ns: Fast backbone motion is mapped by solution 15N relaxation in both redox forms, but only through an abstract: termini, the helix-1/strand-2 linker 20-22 and the active-site-adjacent loops 73-75 and 93-94 are more mobile than average and W31 more than W28 (J1 oxidized, J2 reduced; r1, r2), with side chains spanning a broader range by 13C relaxation (J3, r4) and the Trp indoles constrained (J4, r11, r12; J5 single-Trp mutants; J6 fluorescence, r15, r16). A full-text wild-type R1/R2/NOE set at 20 °C under 1 mM DTT exists only as a figure (J9, r40). The reassembled 1-73/74-108 solid-state construct gives per-residue R1 (0.012-0.636 s-1) and dipolar order parameters (0.35-0.99, mean 0.89) with G21, R73, T14, G33, I4, T66, I72 and H6 most mobile (J10, r6, r7). Weaker: chimera 1M7T S2 0.88 with mobile loops (J8, r45, homolog), fragment complexes (J14), L78K (J20), sub-THz MD (J40).
per_window.us-ms: Redox-dependent and abstract-only. Reduced wild type has an Rex term at 73-75 next to the active site in the 1993 model-free study while the oxidized protein shows no significant mobility there (J15, J16; r3, r1); oxidized wild type shows millisecond motion around the active-site disulfide by 13C/15N relaxation, read as a strained transient disulfide conformation (J17, r5). No CPMG, R1rho or CEST row exists for either redox form and the structured dispersion searches were S. typhi-only (J21, search_insufficient). In the reassembled solid-state construct, cooling to 238 K removes G21, P40, T54 and R73 and broadens most other peaks, read as 10-100 µs motion, and a 400 µs T2' filter keeps A19, D20, G21, R73 strongest (J12, r9, r10; J13 DARR abstract, r31). Fragment-complex R2 elevation at 43-50 and 74-89 (J18) and L78K exchange (J19) are construct inferences.
per_window.slower_than_ms: No native-state rate. The rates in this window are unfolding and refolding kinetics: HDX-MS apparent EX1 unfolding at 50-60 °C in 1% acetic acid, oxidized 0.1 min-1 at 60 °C (EX2 at 50-55 °C) and reduced 0.22, 1.3, 2.5 min-1 (J22, J23; adducts J24), and stopped-flow refolding of reduced wild type from 3.5 M GdmCl with five phases from 75.6 s-1 to 8.7 x 10-4 s-1 (J25; mutants J27).
per_window.undetermined: Hydrogen exchange without a window: native-state HX of oxidized wild type at 25 °C finds no partially unfolded form below global unfolding at 24 probes, with delta-G of opening 4.7-9.9 kcal/mol (J30, r28, r29); redox comparisons localize exchange differences to the active-site sequence, loops 73-75 and 91-98 and the first beta-strand (J31; mutants J32; HDX-MS at 25 °C J33). Structures: the wild-type crystal 2TRX has ten unnamed residues in two conformations (J34), the E101G crystal refines a 50/50 alternate backbone over 10-25, 77-91 and 95-107 (J35, structure_only), other mutant crystals show static local differences (J36), and paired reduced/oxidized NMR structures differ only at the active site (J37). MD: 300 ns wild-type simulation makes persistent transitions at 13-18 (J38; E101G J39). Also here: proline cis/trans two compact forms (J29), oxidized refolding without printed rates (J26), folding-intermediate analysis (J28), aromatic-side-chain MD (J7), CSA averaging faster than ~100 µs in the solid construct (J11), fragment MD (J41), mutant models (J42), Trx-Puf60 fusions (J43), acrylamide quenching (J44, J45), partner mapping and binding kinetics (J46, J47, J48), thermal CD (J49) and C32-adduct exchange at 25 °C (J50). Not judged (no proposition about conformational dynamics of the entry protein): aptamer-scaffold bulk amide 1H T2 of 35 ms (155442-r1); Ni2+-PRE on an HHP-tagged dimer (101601-r23); NOE-based solution-versus-crystal model comparison (101601-r24); global unfolding at 0.02 s-1 in 3.2 M GdmCl (101601-r30); G33 amide visibility and deuteration-dependent linewidths (104151-r5, r10); single-molecule force-clamp reduction kinetics on a substrate (105420-r1, r2) and human-thioredoxin MD (105420-r3, r4, r5); Bacillus subtilis TrxA occupancy on ribonucleotide reductase by cryo-EM and the RNR-tail MD (160402-r15 to r20); human Trx C35S with MsrB1 (160402-r21 to r24); Sphingomonas thioredoxin quenching, bis-ANS and MD (101601-r47 to r52; 160402-r25 to r48). Homolog rows were never used for the reference state.

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Not established at the required level: the only microsecond-millisecond evidence on free wild-type thioredoxin-1 comes from two papers readable as abstracts only, which report an Rex contribution at residues 73-75 (next to the active site) in the reduced dithiol form but no significant exchange there in the oxidized form (1993 15N model-free study), and millisecond motion around the active-site disulfide in the oxidized form by 13C/15N relaxation (1996), with no kex, population, field or temperature available and no CPMG, R1rho or CEST measurement found; the RelaxDB card does not say which redox form was deposited.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: None: the card lists no BMRB id, and the only PDB link (1M7T) is the oxidized human-E. coli chimera, not the entry sequence; no deposition readback exists for TRX.
open_conflicts: Redox form of the RelaxDB sample is unknown from the card; the us-ms answer differs between reduced (Rex at 73-75) and oxidized (none at 73-75, but active-site ms motion by 13C relaxation), so J15/J16/J17 are kept as separate sample states rather than a conflict.

Identity: the card's PDB link 1M7T is the human-E. coli chimera (human 1-66, E. coli 67-106), while the entry sequence is full-length E. coli/S. typhi TrxA; the chimera relaxation (J8) is treated as homolog inference.
questions_for_gina: Which sample produced the RelaxDB TRX relaxation set: reduced or oxidized E. coli thioredoxin (the 1993 Stone et al. data set, which measured both), or the oxidized 1M7T chimera that the card links?
Can the full text of Stone et al. 1993 (10.1021/bi00053a007) and LeMaster 1996 (10.1021/ja960877r) be obtained, since the only us-ms evidence on the wild-type protein sits in their abstracts?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The entry sequence equals mature E. coli TrxA (P0AA25) and S. typhi P0AA29 without Met1, so E. coli thioredoxin-1 rows are the target protein and author numbering equals entry numbering. Redox state is a sample state, not a ligand: every judgment states oxidized (C32-C35 disulfide), reduced (dithiol), or both forms compared. Stone 1993 and LeMaster 1996, the two papers carrying us-ms evidence on the wild type, were readable as abstracts only, so their judgments stay unresolved. The solid-state rows (J10-J12) come from a cleaved 1-73/74-108 reassembly precipitated with PEG-4000 from 10 mM phosphate (final pellet pH not established, redox state unspecified) and are an other-construct inference. HDX-MS rows (J22-J24, J33) are in 1% acetic acid (pH 2.6-2.7) with no pD correction, and the 50-80 °C rows are unfolding, not native-state exchange. Native-state HX (J30) used 30 mM sodium phosphate without a phosphate-free control; the 2017 NMR comparison (J9) used Tris with 1 mM DTT (reduced). Rows r57 and r58 (Trx-Puf60 fusions) are labelled homolog in the CSV although the thioredoxin is E. coli TrxA; they are treated as another construct here. Superseded cases V6_r6_TRX_20261020034041 and V6_r6_TRX_20261020084628 were not used.
